NDT Level III consulting in New Orleans: shipyard, NASA Michoud, refinery and river-terminal programs, and the local options

Around New Orleans, the most demanding NDT programs are in shipbuilding. Navy work brings NAVSEA's NDT requirements, Coast Guard and commercial hulls bring class and owner rules, and the yards in Lockport, Houma and Slidell, with the subcontractors that feed them, need Level IIIs who can work inside those rules. The river refineries and terminals and NASA's Michoud Assembly Facility add requirements of their own. Atlantis supports these companies with ASNT NDT Level III consulting, prepared remotely from Houston, about five and a half hours west by road, with visits for examinations and audits.

What do New Orleans-area companies ask an ASNT Level III for?

  • Shipyards and their subcontractors: written practices, plus MT, UT, PT and VT procedures that meet NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, and the examination and certification records behind them. A recent NDT inspector posting in Lockport asked specifically for MT and UT experience under that publication.
  • Space hardware suppliers to Michoud: programs that answer NASA and prime-contractor flow-down.
  • Refinery and terminal contractors along the river: procedures rewritten for each operator's NDT requirements, with technicians examined and certified before a turnaround begins.
  • Marine repair and offshore fabrication shops working to class society rules, which may need bridging documents between an SNT-TC-1A program and the class requirements.

Louisiana and federal requirements that shape the work

Louisiana's boiler and pressure vessel authority is the Mechanical Safety Section of the State Fire Marshal's office. Louisiana is an NRC Agreement State, and radiography there is done by contractors licensed through the state, not by Atlantis. Naval work adds the NAVSEA publication above, and ASNT runs a separate Naval Shipbuilders NDT Level III certification for Level III examiners contracted into the Huntington Ingalls Newport News or General Dynamics Electric Boat supply chains, applied for through the yard's administrator. If your contract names that certification, confirm the consultant holds it before you engage them.

How the New Orleans options compare

  • IRISNDT lists a Marrero (New Orleans) location among its Louisiana sites, focused on plant inspection.
  • Mistras states that its Level IIIs are certified to NAVSEA 271 as well as SNT-TC-1A and CP-189, and that they can be appointed as a client's Level III.
  • Industrial Service Solutions lists NDE Level III examiners who write written practices, and shipbuilding credentials that include Tech Pub 271 with NAVSEA 250-1500 procedures.
  • In-house Level IIIs at the larger yards, who usually set the bar for subcontractors.
  • Remote outsourced Level IIIs for subcontractors that need SNT-TC-1A program support and records without a resident Level III.

How to vet an NDT Level 3 consultant for Gulf Coast shipyard work

  1. Ask whether the consultant has written procedures under T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, and request a redacted example.
  2. Find out whether your prime requires the ASNT Naval Shipbuilders Level III, and whether the consultant has it.
  3. Confirm the ASNT Level III certificate lists MT, UT, PT and VT if those are your yard methods.
  4. Ask how the consultant keeps objective quality evidence for examinations and vision tests.
  5. If the consultant's employer also supplies inspectors to the same yard, agree in writing who reviews whose work.

For marine repair and offshore yards that also work to class rules, the practical answer is usually one written practice with a bridging document per class society or owner, rather than a separate program for every customer. That keeps one set of certification records, which is what an auditor wants to trace.

How Atlantis supports New Orleans companies

Anoop Rayavarapu, certified ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, prepares written practices and procedures against the document your contract names, and the proposal says plainly where a contract calls for an examiner credential Atlantis does not hold. Drafting is remote; examinations and audits are held at your yard or plant.
